key_insight: Experimentally trained surrogate models can forecast cylinder-wake evolution faster than real time, but they are most reliable only over short horizons and for low-frequency flow structures.
engineering_relevance: This supports practical flow-control and monitoring workflows where quick approximate predictions are valuable, while also highlighting the risk of degraded performance when measurements are noisy, sparse, or incomplete.
method: Trained fully convolutional neural networks, U-Nets, Fourier neural operators, and DMD-based surrogates.
Used two-dimensional, two-component PIV measurements of subcritical cylinder wakes.
Tested both long-horizon forecasting at fixed Re = 590 and multi-Re training from Re = 230 to 2920.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports meaningful short-term predictions and faster-than-real-time evaluation, but reduced preservation of transient features and high-frequency energy under imperfect observations.
watch_item: Performance may drop substantially when extending to more turbulent, three-dimensional, or partially observed flows, so deployment should be cautious outside the measured regime.
paper_title: Data-driven surrogate models for forecasting experimentally measured fluid flows
